findings.title: Optimized audit-log pagination cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to the AuditLogEntry.datetime value. Those functions do not accept datetime objects, so an optimized request with any results raises TypeError while building its cursors. value_from_cursor also returns a numeric value rather than converting it to a datetime for subsequent queries. Use DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversion logic for this endpoint.

findings.title: Negative offsets are not supported by Django querysets
findings.body: The advanced-features branch passes a negative start directly to QuerySet slicing. Django rejects negative indices with ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), rather than handling the boundary automatically as the comment claims. An optimized pagination request with a cursor such as '0:-1:0' therefore fails instead of returning a page. Reject invalid offsets as a pagination error or normalize them before slicing.

findings.title: Changing existing Redis set keys to sorted sets requires a migration
findings.body: The buffer now issues ZADD and ZSCAN against the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous implementation populated with SADD. Existing buffered segments remain Redis sets, so new ingestion into those keys and flushing them will fail with WRONGTYPE after deployment. Mixed-version consumers also cannot read each other's buffers. Introduce a versioned key namespace with a drain strategy, or explicitly migrate/drain existing keys before switching commands, to avoid blocking processing and losing buffered segments.
